items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: Lee Codden was a blues player.

ctx.x: But when he's bucking somebody, what number would he play? Did he have a real crip that he could beat him with?

Oh, he played, I'mma tell you, man. That guy, he was a good first-style guy. He played sweet numbers. He stayed at now. Oh, he had something to run him with, no? Mm-hmm. Yeah, man. He could play the blues better than any, any trumpet play any time. Mm-hmm. Lee Codden was a blues player. Mm-hmm. But, he could take that mute, the rubber, you know, that flushing. Mm-hmm. When he get that thing up, he'd stand up in that truck. He'd go on it. Going back home to Jamaica, now he could play that.
